memos.headline: Defensive Leadership Persists: PG and AAPL Hold Trend While NVDA and AMZN Break Down Hard
memos.body: I see a clear bifurcation in this universe as of March 7. PG is the standout leader—only 2.1% off its 52-week high, trading 5.2% above its 50-day and 4.2% above its 200-day, with relative strength vs SPY of +9.2% over 4 weeks and +6.5% over 12 weeks. AAPL is the only mega-cap tech name holding its ground, sitting right at its 50-day mean with positive relative strength (+7.5% 4w, +3.7% 12w). On the other side, NVDA is in freefall—down 24.6% from its high, 14.5% below its 50-day, RSI 37.8, and hemorrhaging relative strength at -15.6% over 12 weeks; I would need to see it reclaim 125 (roughly the 50-day area) before reconsidering. AMZN's RSI of 29.8 is the lowest in the group and it has lost 16.6% in four weeks, but catching this knife requires a close back above 210 at minimum. JPM's sharp 8.5% weekly drop pushed RSI to 30.3, but the longer-term trend above the 200-day (+6.7%) keeps me from outright avoiding it—I'd watch 235 as a line in the sand.

views.note: Strongest relative strength in the universe (+9.2% 4w vs SPY), near 52w highs, above both moving averages; would reassess on a break below 170.
Holding at the 50-day mean with best 4w relative strength among mega-cap tech (+7.5% vs SPY); a close below 230 would flip me neutral.
Down 24.6% from highs, 14.5% below 50-day, RSI 37.8, and worst 12w relative strength in the group at -15.6%; need a reclaim of ~125 to reconsider.
RSI 29.8 is deeply oversold and 4w return of -16.6% signals capitulation, but no sign of stabilization yet; need a close above 210 to consider a bounce trade.
Trading 5.8% below 50-day and 7.5% below 200-day with negative 12w relative strength of -6.1%; trend is clearly down, would need a reclaim of 410 to turn neutral.
Sharp weekly selloff (-8.5%) pushed RSI to 30.3, but still 6.7% above 200-day and 12w relative strength is positive; watching 235 as support.
Flat at the 50-day with decent 4w relative strength (+5.6% vs SPY) but below the 200-day by 4.6%; no strong directional signal here.
Down 21.1% from highs and 9.5% below 200-day in a persistent downtrend over 26 weeks; last week's bounce is not enough to change the picture.
Sitting near both moving averages with a neutral RSI of 49.1 but 12w return of -11.3% and weak relative strength; no edge either way until it breaks 365 or loses 335.
Bounced last week (+2.1%) but still 7.8% below 50-day and 15.8% off highs; 12w relative strength is positive but 4w is negative—mixed signals.

memos.headline: NVDA and GOOGL Show Strongest Earnings Power; XOM and UNH Flash Margin Warnings
memos.body: I see the clearest durable earnings power in NVDA (+77.9% YoY revenue, 56.2% net margin) and GOOGL (+11.8% revenue, 27.5% margin with only $14.8B debt), both delivering accelerating profitability on manageable leverage. MSFT continues to compound at +12.3% revenue growth with a 34.6% net margin and moderate $45B debt load, making it a reliable compounder. On the other side, XOM posted -1.1% revenue decline with a thin 9.1% net margin, and UNH grew revenue only 6.8% while net income barely moved (+1.6%) on a heavy $76.9B debt stack—both signal cash-flow compression risk. CAT's -5.0% revenue decline is a concern, though margin expansion to 17.2% and +4.4% net income growth show cost discipline; I need to see the top line stabilize before getting constructive. PG's +33.5% net income jump on only +2.1% revenue is impressive margin management, but the low organic growth ceiling limits upside.

views.note: 77.9% YoY revenue growth and 56.2% net margin on just $8.5B debt is extraordinary earnings power; would reassess if gross margins compress below 50%.
11.8% revenue growth, 27.5% net margin, and minimal $14.8B debt make this the best risk-adjusted earnings profile among mega-caps; a deceleration in Cloud or Search revenue would change my view.
12.3% revenue growth and 34.6% net margin with $45B debt is a durable compounder; I'd turn cautious if Azure growth decelerates materially.
Net income nearly doubled YoY to $20B on 10.5% revenue growth, pushing margin to 10.7%—margin trajectory is the key variable to watch.
Only +4.0% revenue growth with $94.8B in debt is the weakest top-line profile among big tech despite a solid 29.2% margin; need to see Services mix accelerate.
50.5% net income growth and 32.7% margin are strong but likely peak-cycle; credit loss provisions would be the line item to watch.
Impressive 33.5% net income growth on just 2.1% revenue growth reflects margin gains that may not repeat; organic volume growth is the swing factor.
Revenue declining 1.1% with a 9.1% net margin and $36.8B debt signals earnings vulnerability to further commodity weakness.
Only 1.6% net income growth on 6.8% revenue growth with $76.9B debt and a 5.5% margin points to cost pressures eroding earnings power.
Top-line contraction of -5.0% is concerning despite margin resilience at 17.2%; I need revenue to stabilize before turning constructive.

memos.headline: Fed on Pause at 4.50% With Sticky 3% CPI — Favor Defensives and Banks Over Duration-Sensitive Growth
memos.body: I see the Fed firmly in pause mode: the upper bound sits at 4.50%, down 100bp over 12 months but unchanged since the last 25bp cut, while CPI is running at 3.0% YoY — well above target and re-accelerating (+1.1% over just three months). The labor market remains resilient with unemployment at 4.0%, ticking down 10bp over the quarter, giving the Fed no urgency to ease further. The 10y-2y spread has steepened sharply to +33bp (up 77bp YoY), and the 10y yield at 4.32% has risen 17bp over three months, signaling the market is pricing out near-term cuts and embedding a term premium. In this regime — rates on hold, sticky inflation, solid employment — I favor banks (wider NIM from steeper curve) and defensive staples over long-duration growth names whose valuations are pressured by elevated real rates. A CPI print falling below 2.5% YoY or unemployment breaching 4.3% would shift my call toward an easing regime favoring growth.

views.note: Steepening curve (+77bp YoY in 10y-2y spread) and 4.50% fed funds support net interest margins; pause regime is the sweet spot for large banks.
Defensive staple with pricing power benefits from a late-cycle pause regime where growth is decelerating but inflation stays elevated.
Long-duration growth name most exposed to rising real rates; 10y yield up 23bp YoY and no near-term easing catalyst pressures rich multiples.
Duration-sensitive but strong cash generation provides some buffer; I stay neutral until the rate path clarifies.
Quality growth with recurring revenue mitigates rate risk, but 4.32% 10y yield caps multiple expansion — no strong macro edge either way.
Resilient labor market supports demand, but sticky inflation and a pause regime offer no clear macro tailwind for energy; staying neutral.
Cyclical bellwether faces mixed signals: employment is solid but rate-sensitive capex may stall with the Fed on hold at 4.50%.
Blended consumer/cloud exposure; elevated rates weigh on growth multiple but consumer spending remains supported by low unemployment.
Ad revenue tied to nominal GDP which is fine, but no macro catalyst to go overweight with rates elevated and no easing in sight.
Defensive healthcare with stable cash flows benefits in a pause regime; less rate-sensitive than growth tech.

memos.headline: Post-Earnings Sentiment Washout Across Mega-Cap Tech Creates Selective Opportunity; Defensives Hold Up
memos.body: I am struck by the uniformly negative post-earnings price reactions across the large-cap tech and growth complex this cycle: NVDA -8.5%, GOOGL -7.3%, MSFT -6.2%, AMZN -4.1%, and even CAT -4.6% and UNH -6.0%. The severity and breadth of these sell-offs suggest crowded positive positioning heading into prints, meaning the negative tone shift was amplified by positioning unwinds rather than purely fundamental disappointment. By contrast, JPM (+2.0%) and PG (+1.9%) posted positive reactions, indicating sentiment was not stretched in those names and the narrative remains constructive. With several weeks having passed since the worst reactions (NVDA's -8.5% drop was just last week on 2/27), I see the most interesting contrarian tone-reversal setup in names where the negative reaction was sharpest and most recent, though I have higher conviction in the defensives where sentiment never soured.

views.note: Positive earnings reaction (+2.0%) and steady stream of corporate governance filings suggest constructive narrative with no crowding.
Positive post-earnings reaction (+1.9%) and dividend announcement signal stable defensive sentiment that is not yet crowded.
The -8.5% post-earnings drop on 2/27 is the most severe and most recent washout; tone may be bottoming but it is too fresh to call a reversal with conviction.
The -7.3% earnings reaction was harsh and occurred over a month ago, so some negative sentiment may be priced, but I lack evidence of a clear tone inflection.
A -6.2% post-earnings drop signals a meaningful negative narrative shift around cloud growth expectations that likely has not fully washed through sentiment.
The -6.0% earnings reaction in mid-January points to a durable negative tone shift in managed care sentiment that I do not see reversing yet.
Mild -0.7% earnings reaction suggests sentiment was balanced; no strong signal in either direction from available evidence.
The -4.6% post-earnings drop reflects a negative industrial cycle narrative that likely persists given macro uncertainty.

memos.headline: Policy Uncertainty Doubles in Three Months; Export-Control and Tariff Risk Weighs on Tech and Industrials
memos.body: I am writing with the economic policy uncertainty index at 726 — nearly double its level three months ago (+85.9%) and up 95% in just one month — while the VIX has surged to 24.87 (+94.8% over three months). This is not a one-quarter blip; the magnitude and persistence of the move signals a structural escalation in trade and sanctions policy risk, likely tied to broadening tariff actions and tightening export controls on advanced semiconductors. High-yield spreads have widened 33 bps over the past month to 2.99%, confirming that credit markets are beginning to price in real economic drag. WTI crude at $66.62 is down 6.1% month-over-month, suggesting demand-side concern is outweighing any supply-disruption premium, which is notable for energy names. I have highest conviction that NVDA faces the most concentrated geopolitical headwind given its China AI-chip exposure, while PG's defensive profile and limited policy surface area make it the relative safe harbor in this environment.

views.note: Export-control tightening on advanced AI chips to China is a structural headwind; policy uncertainty at 726 and NVDA's 8-K filing in January suggest ongoing regulatory engagement.
Supply-chain concentration in China and rising tariff/trade-war risk at current policy uncertainty levels make AAPL vulnerable to further escalation.

Tariff risk cuts both ways for CAT — potential infrastructure spending tailwind domestically but input-cost and retaliatory-tariff headwinds abroad; I need clarity on next trade-policy actions to take a directional view.
Defensive consumer staples with diversified global supply chain and limited direct exposure to export controls; a relative haven when policy uncertainty is at 726.
WTI at $66.62 and falling 6.1% m/m suggests demand fears dominate despite geopolitical supply risks; energy security narrative could flip this but I lack conviction today.
Widening HY spreads (+33 bps) and steepening curve (+9 bps m/m) are mixed for banks; sanctions-related compliance costs add friction but NIM benefits from steeper curve.
Antitrust and China policy risks are real but less acute than for hardware-exposed tech; staying neutral until regulatory actions crystallize.

plan.summary: Elevated policy uncertainty (EPU 726), sticky inflation, and a Fed on pause favor defensive positioning centered on PG (consensus long across 4 of 5 analysts) and JPM (macro + sentiment support from steepening curve and positive earnings reaction). We keep a large cash buffer (~45%) given VIX near 25 and broad tech breakdowns, adding only modest positions in GOOGL and AAPL where fundamental or technical support exists but conflicts limit sizing.

plans.rationale: Strongest consensus across all five analysts: Technical (0.85 long, best relative strength +9.2% 4w), Sentiment (positive +1.9% earnings reaction), Macro (defensive haven in pause regime), Geopolitics (safe harbor at EPU 726). Fundamentals note margin gains but flags low organic growth, keeping us from exceeding max weight.
plans.changes_my_mind: Weekly close below 170 (50-day support area) or a sharp reversal in relative strength vs SPY turning negative over 2 weeks.

plans.rationale: Macro analyst is most bullish (0.75) citing steepening yield curve (+77bp YoY) supporting NIM; Sentiment analyst (0.70) notes positive +2.0% earnings reaction and constructive narrative. Technical analyst is neutral given sharp -8.5% weekly drop to RSI 30.3 but notes still above 200-day. Sizing down from mechanical seed due to technical weakness and geopolitical analyst's neutral stance on widening HY spreads.
plans.changes_my_mind: Weekly close below 235 (Technical analyst's line in the sand) or HY spreads widening above 3.5% signaling credit stress.

plans.rationale: Fundamentals analyst is strongly bullish (0.80) citing 11.8% revenue growth, 27.5% net margin, and minimal debt — best risk-adjusted earnings profile among mega-caps. Technical and sentiment analysts are neutral/mixed, and geopolitics analyst sees moderate antitrust risk. Sized modestly due to conflicting signals: still 7.8% below 50-day technically but fundamentals are compelling.
plans.changes_my_mind: Weekly close below 165 (roughly another 5% down) or evidence of material Cloud/Search revenue deceleration in next data points.

plans.rationale: Technical analyst is constructive (0.65 long) noting AAPL holds its 50-day with best 4w relative strength in mega-cap tech. However, Fundamentals analyst is only neutral (weak 4% revenue growth), Geopolitics analyst flags China supply-chain risk at current EPU levels (0.65 avoid), and Sentiment sees no strong signal. Minimal sizing reflects these conflicts.
plans.changes_my_mind: Weekly close below 230 (Technical analyst's flip level) or escalation of China tariff/trade actions specifically targeting consumer electronics.
